input_text: EDIT: While initially I didn't recommend, I do think the game is good and I was a bit too harsh. The game has potential, is updated regularly, and the developer is receptive to input. That is all anyone could ask for in a game. Something that I forgot to mention was that the gameplay loop is relatively quick, which I think is a strength. Games take 5-10 minutes each and are a good way to kill time. Also, the recent update made the black holes much more manageable. Big win in my eyes as it felt like an auto loss before when they spawned I look forward to where the game goes. ------------------ Novi Cube is a neat concept but suffers from poor execution. The level up mechanic is flawed. You pick one of three random traits offered and have the option to reroll for a "token", something you get for clearing bosses. However, a bunch of these traits are useless. Projectile size does basically nothing. Explosive tiles are ineffective against bosses. There is a very clear meta that forms as you attempt higher difficulties. I find myself taking the same upgrades every time because everything else just doesn't have the damage. Not only that but the black hole enemy sucks out all the fun you might have. It exerts gravity, eats your shots and is invulnerable so you are essentially helpless if it spawns. It doesn't even give you anything if you survive it. God help you if the game decides to position you right under it, you will never be able to break any tiles. Did I forget to mention that you can't even control where you shoot from?

input_text: This is one of those VR games where when you first start it up, you think it could be pretty cool. That is, if you get past being stuck in the intro loading screen. But when you really get into the gameplay, you realize just how bad it really is. There are only four levels in this game they all look EXACTLY the same, which is a confusing maze of dark empty dull corridors. There is also an issue with the enemies because they all zigzag quickly towards you if you are seen. You then end up firing arrows at point blank range because they are always right up in your face. There is also no way to manually save the game and you can only take a few hits from their extremely accurate arrow shots or hits from a sword until you die. So you are then forced to restart the entire level. This game has all the indications of an early VR game that has been abandoned by the developer. There are much better archery VR options out there such as In Death, QuiVR, Lone Archer, and Wrath of the Fire God.

input_text: The first "horror" experience I tried on my Vive. From the moment I started in the room where you choose your locomotion mechanic, I was hooked. I've played it a number of times since, and thoroughly enjoyed the feeling of the hairs on my neck as it unfolds. I'm running it on a G1-1070 and it looks sweet, although the black elements could do with a little work as the HMD has a strange grey output in full black which feels like diving through barely visible soup The only negative is the full locomotion option - it took me time to work out how to avoid simulator sickness, making sure to face forward whenever moving, and also rocking my head slightly from side to side to trick my vestibular system into thinking I am walking - its crude but works, and helped me enjoy this game (and other games with full locom) without suffering any nausea effects. This is a very effective piece of work, and the complimentary demo shows great potential for the full experience.
